record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the same lubrication approximation of an axisymmetric liquid jet before droplet breakup, do solutions remain consistent with the asymptotic approximation by retaining a bounded first spatial derivative of the radius h up to the pinch-off time?

evidence.quote: A conjecture due to CONSTANTIN states that before breakup solutions to (1) retain bounded first derivative in h.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the lubrication approximation for an axisymmetric liquid jet driven by surface tension prior to droplet breakup. Let h(z,t) > 0 denote the radius of the free surface of the jet as a function of axial coordinate z and time t, satisfying the standard one-dimensional lubrication system governing the evolution of h and the axial velocity, derived as an asymptotic reduction of the free-surface Navier–Stokes (or Euler) equations under the assumption that the slope ∂h/∂z is small. Let T* < ∞ denote the pinch-off time, i.e., the first time at which inf_z h(z,t) → 0.

Prove or disprove the following conjecture: for solutions of this lubrication system starting from smooth initial data with bounded slope, the first spatial derivative ∂h/∂z remains uniformly bounded on [0,T*), so that the slope-smallness assumption underlying the lubrication asymptotics remains consistent with the solution up to the pinch-off time.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any published proof or disproof of Constantin's conjecture concerning boundedness of ∂h/∂z up to pinch-off in the axisymmetric jet lubrication model. Related work on thin-film lubrication regularity (Bertozzi–Pugh and others) and on droplet breakup singularities exists, but none of the retrieved results directly resolve this specific conjecture, so the status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: The lubrication approximation for thin viscous films: Regularity and long-time behavior of weak solutions
status_evidence.snippet: Regularity results for thin-film lubrication equations, related context but not addressing the axisymmetric jet slope-boundedness conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Related regularity literature does not directly resolve the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Capillary pinch-off in liquid-in-liquid systems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on pinch-off dynamics in axisymmetric liquid columns.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on pinch-off but the specific conjecture remains unaddressed in retrieved sources.
